# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 46 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 46 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_046_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 3 — The Compassionate Lord and His Two Angels

**46:1** "Lord," I said, "now that I've reached the end of these commandments, let me ask: is it actually possible for anyone to keep them? They're so demanding and so serious." "You will keep them," he said, "if your heart is pure before God. Everyone who has cleared their heart of the empty cravings of this world will keep them and will truly live for God."

**46:2** "Lord," I said, "but what about someone who genuinely wants to keep these commandments but can't manage it because their body is weak? What happens to them?" "If they take them on but don't follow through, and their heart turns away from the Lord — that person is heading for death. But someone who takes them on with their whole heart, who works hard to do right, even though they stumble sometimes because of bodily weakness — that person will live, because the Lord is compassionate."

**46:3** "The Lord sees that person's heart is pure and takes pity on them, forgiving all their stumbling and wandering. He strengthens them and enables them to keep the commandments of the Angel of Righteousness, and through that brings them to salvation."

**46:4** "But for someone who lives carelessly, forgetting God and ignoring his commandments — the Lord hands that person over to the angel of punishment, who torments them for their wickedness. That torment is corrective — it aims at their salvation."

**46:5** "But lord," I said, "how can the Lord be so full of compassion and at the same time allow such punishment?" "Listen," he said. "The Lord shows compassion in everything he does and everything he says. He is full of love for humanity, gentleness, patience, and mercy. So as long as someone is capable of repenting, there is hope. But when a person completely turns away from God and keeps sinning with no repentance — there is no hope for that person."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the pastoral balance of judgment and compassion in Mandate 12.*
